text_fidelity_a:
Garmin nüvi 255W 4.3-Inch Portable GPS Navigator (Discontinued by Manufacturer) I purchased this GPS as a Christmas present for my brother who wanted an accurate device without the bells and whistles. So far it has met or exceeded expectations.

This GPS is incredibly easy to install and highly accurate. The display is clear and bright and the robotic voice instructions are a help. Programming is a snap and the time of arrival has been dead on. the basic tool options are present including world clock, where am I? and points of interest. The points of interest do seem a bit limited so it helps to have the actual address if you are visitng a specific location that might be off the beaten track. Unfortuneately the implement that is supposed to hold lthe device to the dash is useless. It is flimsy and does not adhere for more than a few seconds. So avoid the annoyance and just buy one that works.

I have a 3790T and love it. However, I could not live without the voice command and have come to rely on the bluetooth for my cell phone. But for an inexpensive, reliable unit with just the basics, this device is a good choice.
text_fidelity_b: Garmin nüvi 255W 4.3-Inch Portable GPS Navigator (Discontinued by Manufacturer)

text_fidelity_a:
Cisco-Linksys E3000 Wireless-N Router I bought this router in December, 2010 to replace my Linksys WRT54GS wireless router. I was a bit surprised to find that there are no external antennae and no place to install one on the E3000, but I haven't encountered any problems with signal. This router hasn't bottlenecked once, whereas my WRT54GS would bottleneck if the wind blew wrong. The only time I have unplugged this router was because I had to reconfigure it from scratch when I discovered I couldn't configure any of the settings using the built-in software once I'd changed the router configuration in the browser config pages. I read some work-arounds in the Amazon.com reviews and had to reset to factory defaults. I had to fully uninstall and reinstall the Cisco Connect software as well. As long as you go through that software first and THEN make adjustments in your advanced configuration settings via your web browser, you can still access things like parental control and guest wifi security. If you change your router's address, however, from 192.168.1.1 to anything different, expect to never be able to get into Cisco Connect again. The only reason I can envision needing the Cisco Connect software is to access the guest wifi and the parental controls, so if you don't need those things, don't worry about making changes you normally would via the browser interface.

The wifi button on the router is handy for setting up wireless devices such as cell phones and internet tablets, it hooks right up to your wireless network and you don't have to rely on the guest access to connect. You will also have the ability to set up a physical key using a USB thumb drive (you must provide your own) for setting up other computers on your wifi network, which works like a charm. It is especially compatible with the Cisco-Linksys WUSB600N Dual-Band Wireless-N USB Network Adapter, which I also highly recommend. I haven't tried the networked storage option yet due to the location of my router in relation to my external drives, but it is definitely an option that I will look into setting up some day.

I would say this router is worth the $150 I paid for it (locally), with the biggest reason being that so far I haven't been able to bottleneck it, even with my 60MB cable service, wireless-connected computers, Wii, and other various wireless devices. Cisco/Linksys really did a good thing with this model and I'm quite pleased with it; it is definitely worth the price.
text_fidelity_b: Cisco-Linksys E3000 Wireless-N Router

text_fidelity_a:
SAMSUNG Galaxy S9+ Factory Unlocked Smartphone 64GB - Midnight Black I had a Galaxy S4 for several years. It was suitable and did the job. . . mostly. I was having some battery issues and my phone wouldn't update past Android 4.4. I was running into apps that needed a newer version of Android. I could have bought something cheap but I decided to treat myself and found the blue Galaxy S9 on sale for a decent price. I have to say I'm loving this phone.
The 5.8" Quad HD+ Super AMOLED screen is GLORIOUS! I run this is high performance mode with the brightness cranked up. Games, movies, even YouTube and TikTok videos look amazing. The curved edge I worried might be distracting but honestly I only notice in a couple games.
Sound is really good for a cell phone it has stereo speakers. Volume is more than enough.
Performance from the Octa-Core processor and 4GB of ram have not struggled to run anything I've thrown at it.
The camera is great. Maybe struggling a little in very bright light with a light colored subject. Otherwise, night mode gives great low light results. Video shooting is very nice with great slow motion results and a nearly unique super slow-motion recording mode at a mind boggling 960 frames per second is a lot of fun to mess around with.
Battery life is good, I got most of a day is high performance mode and could easily extend it by cutting things back to save battery.
The fingerprint sensor is quick to unlock and easy to use. A trick I found online to improve performance of the fingerprint sensor is to register the same finger more than once. It really works like a charm.
The look is sleek and sophisticated though I'm protecting that glass body with a nice Otterbox Symmetry case. The only real minor negative to the whole thing is this weighs more and is larger than my S4, a little hard on my hands and pocket but really, it's worth it.
I can't express how happy I am with this phone. I'm even buying props and things to use in creative videos and photo shoots.
text_fidelity_b: SAMSUNG Galaxy S9+ Factory Unlocked Smartphone 64GB - Midnight Black

Open the box and you'll find attractively packaged (hint hint to someone thinking of getting these as a gift) headphones as well as a round case with a zipper matching the color. Later it was connected to my PC while cruising new tunes. Lest you think they are only for EDM, they really enhance gaming as well.
Then I compared them to my old but loved Lady GaGa Monster Beats, as well as a few lower end headsets. Granted the Beats are getting a little wonky, but I have to say it's better to be in the MEE EDM Universe. Can't help but notice logo similarity, hmmmm.

My mother was great lover of opera and symphony. I grew up listening to her records, and when I was small I'd ask her to put on Ravel's Bolero and I'd lie down, listening to it build.
Need to get out of your skin for a while? Put these on, lie down flat on your back. Hit play, close your eyes, palms up, and just absorb everything.

Now THAT'S kandi for the soul.

text_fidelity_a:
Roku Express | Easy High Definition (HD) Streaming Media Player (2018) I received this Roku Express for review, but honestly, I just now installed it and I can't tell any difference between it and my previous Roku Express I got about a year and a half ago. It streams exactly the same as far as I can tell, but it streams very well. It was a bit of a pain to install since the Roku site refused my password and the instructions afterwards aren't all that easy to follow if you lose your password. But, after plugging in all my passwords for internet connection, Netflix, Amazon, etc...it finally started streaming again. I can't tell that it's any faster. Nonetheless, if you don't have a Roku and want to stream a boatload of free channels with movies and lots of other cool stuff to watch, I suggest getting a Roku. You can add paid channels later. And Roku doesn't require a credit card to use.

It comes with a short HDMI cable and everything you need to get streaming. As far as the actual hardware installation, it's extremely easy. It takes less than 10 seconds to put it on top of the TV and connect the 2 cables (HDMI and power). A sticky tape comes to adhere the Roku to the top of the TV since the Roku is so small it tends to fall off with being stuck. This is my 3rd Roku and we rarely watch regular TV anymore.
This Roku will stream in 1080 and 720 psi. I had ordered about 5 or so generic Roku remotes earlier this year since we tend to lose them and one of our dogs has chewed up the original remotes beyond usage, and they all work fine with this Roku.

Roku is always good, just a little bit of a pain to get past all the passwords, codes and stuff in the beginning, especially if your old password for some reason doesn't work anymore.

text_fidelity_a:
Motorola T200TP Talkabout Radio, 3 Pack This is a nice little set of radios, improved from my last three-pack of similarly priced Motorolas, but has some room for improvement.

Goods:

+ Good size - small enough, but big enough to fit in your hand comfortably like a radio should. Yes, it could be smaller, but at some point you don't really want smaller.

+ Some basic options to customize, mostly the noises the radios make. LCD screen shows you what you need to know.

+ Batteries can be charged while in the radios via standard Micro USB adapters - two are included. One charges one radio while the other charges two simultaneously.

+ Belt clip included. Head sets can be added.

Bad:

- While it's great that the battery packs can be charged via USB and the chargers are accepted worldwide (whereas my previous set for work had barrel connections to the charger and I burnt one out the first night I tried to charge due to being in Europe, the battery/charger setup is still imperfect for two reasons:

1) Battery packs are not three separate batteries that could be charged with other chargers and switched with other batteries (think Eneloop). My Garmin topo GPS came with actual rechargeable batteries that could be used elsewhere. This makes sense when you want to be able to carry standard alkaline batteries for emergencies/backup. These battery packs are great that they can be replaced with AA when necessary, but not as good as standard, replaceable rechargeable batteries (but you can use rechargeable batteries as your backup batteries).

2) N-MH doesn't make sense for this application because these are the type of batteries that develop a "memory". If you use these every day for work, then you want to recharge them every night. Actually, you would be inclined to recharge every time you want to use them, period, to be sure you get the most from the batteries. But because of the memory, you really want to discharge them fully. The appropriate type of battery would be Li-ion, because they would be chargeable every night AND would last longer. This is the biggest negative to this rig. If the battery packs were Li-ion, I would not care that they are packs versus separate batteries.

- Belt clip should be taken off to remove battery cover without beating the two up. This is apparently an obvious issue to the manufacturer because they have a protective piece of plastic between the two for shipment.

Neutral (strange):

Two standard USB chargers included, at 500mA output each (1A would be minimum standard and expected these days, but whatever; they may have done this to avoid overcharging overnight). Both have the same rated input, but the output is the same (samex2 on the 2 output charger). That actually doesn't make sense, unless the single charger is half as efficient (or they are just too lazy to change the nameplate). Not really sure what's up with that, but I sort of like the 2-output charger. I expect most people have so many USB chargers laying around that they'll use whatever is at hand anyway vice these.
text_fidelity_b: Motorola T200TP Talkabout Radio, 3 Pack

I had turned it off, but as soon as I rebooted, it came on and stayed that way. The wires don't seem to be easily accessible to unplug it. Winegard FL5500A FlatWave Amped Digital HD Indoor Amplified TV Antenna (4K Ready / ATSC 3.0 Ready / High-VHF / UHF), 60 Mile Long Range, Black/White, 6 Feet Got this on Amazon Lightning Deal for $50 but it's just not worth that much, IMO, so I'll be returning it. I do live on the bottom floor of a 3-story apartment building that's built into a hill (so 2 stories on the other side), with a patch of pine trees in front of me, so I fully understand that there are many hurdles for my particular set up. However, I also live in a major city, not 30 miles from all the broadcast towers, and while this antenna can pick up those channels, it's incredibly inconsistent at holding the signal. Pictures do a slight pixelation maybe every five minutes or so; nothing major, but enough to be annoying, and so I don't think this particular antenna is worth fifty bucks - I feel like I could get that same level of "service" from a cheap-y model. I also am using the amplifier.

As far as decor - it's non-obtrusive, and has a long cable so finding good placement for best reception is pretty easy.

My mom snagged one of the Amazon-version ones for $25 a few hours later in the Lightning Deals. I could see paying $25 for this, simply because it's less gaudy than rabbit ears, but not because I believe you're getting anything more reception-wise.
text_fidelity_b: Winegard FL5500A FlatWave Amped Digital HD Indoor Amplified TV Antenna (4K Ready / ATSC 3.0 Ready / High-VHF / UHF), 60 Mile Long Range, Black/White, 6 Feet

text_fidelity_a:
Epson E11E223052 ProSense 367 GPS Multisport Watch with Ultra Long Battery Life and Sapphire Glass - Black I run during the summer and run outside. I hate carrying heavy items with me, like water bottles and phones. I feel they sort of hinder my performance, though I realize it's probably more psychological than physical.
Still, I'm not going to mess with a run I've been accustomed to for nearly twenty years, but I do wish, more often than not, that I had some way of tracking my run and how many miles I've done *exactly* while being outside. Sure, I can track the mileage by checking my phone before and after, but it would be nice to have a tracker on me without adding any psychological weight. I used to have a Polar watch that worked fine, but it died some time ago and I never bothered to get a replacement.
But finally I did.

With this one, I'm able to wear the watch without toting my phone along and it still carries all the features and tracking as if the phone were connected to any other tracking watch. While this watch is used for a number of cardio activities, I use it only for running. There are "pages" of exercises you can track, but for a quick run the default is set on the bottom left button--very nice to have, especially for me. Not sure if you can change the default on there to another exercise, but for me it's perfect and I haven't bothered looking up how to change it.
But curious to check out the full features, I ventured into the different pages (or screens) the watch has to offer. During my course, I found that the buttons were *very* stiff. This might be to prevent accidental presses during exercise, but I found that I had to press almost twice has hard as other electronic watches for the watch to recognize my press. But, from my uses so far, I've pressed it mostly to view all the screens when testing out all the features. When actually running, I do no more than a few presses before and after each run. The network had trouble activating itself in the beginning, but that's because I was fiddling with it outside. It kept trying to set itself numerous times when I actually ran outside, but I always dismissed it. Once, however, I was under the open sky I let it connect and it has had no problem or delay connecting ever since.

After every run I am able to sync it with the Epson app, as well as RunKeeper. People have complained about the Epson app but I find it neat and useful.

Overall, it's a great little watch that accurately records my runs and uploads them without the use of the phone during the workout. I'm able to review it speedily on my phone right after, and I love that I can now track my progress without the burden of added weight. It's pricey for sure, but considering I don't need my phone and my previous watch lasted me ten years, I'm sure this watch will be a great investment that will last me hopefully for another decade or so.
text_fidelity_b: Epson E11E223052 ProSense 367 GPS Multisport Watch with Ultra Long Battery Life and Sapphire Glass - Black

text_fidelity_a:
Netgear WGR614 Wireless-G Router We bought this Netgear WGR614 router back in March 2006. It installed somewhat easily and except for a little problem with the wireless PC card for the laptop (wouldn't be recognized at first but easily corrected) we had pretty stable use for about a year. Then we began to have connection problems. The connection would get slower and slower until internet pages would just not load, resulting in repeated "page cannot be displayed" errors. Powering down and restarting the router, modem and computer seemed to correct the issue. But as of this morning the router appears to have completely died. Powering down and restarting does nothing, the internet connection cannot be re-established. We can connect the desktop directly to the cable modem but for now the laptop is without connection, making for some unhappy family members here.

As of right now I don't know if we'll be buying another Netgear router & wireless PC card. The life expectancy of Netgear products does not appear to be all that great. Looking at some of the reviews we appear to be quite lucky that we got as much time out of the router as we did. Still I'm not in the mood to be shopping for a new router every 1.5 years or less. Hopefully there is a good router out there that can last at least two years.
text_fidelity_b: Netgear WGR614 Wireless-G Router

Dell Inspiron 14 Plus 7420 Laptop - 14 inch, 2.2K 16:10, Intel Core i7-12700H, 16GB DDR5 RAM, 1TB SSD, Intel Iris Xe, 2 Yr Onsite + AntiVirus, Migrate, Windows 11 Pro+Office 365 - Atlantic Green The Dell Inspiron 14 Plus 7420 Laptop, what a sleek little machine. It has a nice slate grey color with a matte finish. It is thin, it is powerful, and it just fits what my wife uses it for, which is some office work (word, excel, emails) and some media consumption (videos, social media, etc). Pretty much what everyone would need a laptop for.

Unfortunately, I'm unable to test this computer to its fullest with some games or video editing because I haven't been able to pry it away from my wife since she got it.

Looking simply at the specs of this machine, it is obvious that the i7 12th generation with the Intel Iris integrated graphics will be able to handle anything a casual user would be able to throw at it. The 16gb of ram will handle a LOT of browser windows and application being open at the same time. The 1tb ssd is actually great to have considering that many laptops only include half of this storage. Lastly, the 2.2K resolution is perfect for this small 14" screen. It's higher than full-hd 1080p and isn't too high to where the text and icons are barely legible.

The keyboard is the standard chiclet keys with good travel. It is quite and works well enough to not cause typos or missed key presses.

The screen is comfortable to look at and at 14" it allows this laptop to be a great portable workhorse.

Overall, I'm impressed with the stability, comfort, and just the build quality of this product. With the powerful CPU, I expect that this machine can last for quite a few years.
text_fidelity_b: Dell Inspiron 14 Plus 7420 Laptop - 14 inch, 2.2K 16:10, Intel Core i7-12700H, 16GB DDR5 RAM, 1TB SSD, Intel Iris Xe, 2 Yr Onsite + AntiVirus, Migrate, Windows 11 Pro+Office 365 - Atlantic Green

We hang all of the important cords on there for charging and recharging our appliances that need cords. Over time this has gotten WAY out of hand. I wanted to have a place to put the cords away and still have access to them.

ZIPPERS
The zippers are two way and work great.

COMPARTMENTS
The compartments hold quite a few cords. I know that this is for travel, but for me, I keep this near the hooks in the cord area and it is small and easy to store. The elastics hold quite a few sets of cords and the pockets hold even more. The small cases are great for ear buds and the other cases are good for extra cards, etc.

ROOM FOR TABLET?
This does have a nice spot for a tablet. Having it in a sleeve would not be a bad idea though due to the other items in the case.

DOES IT HOLD A LOT?
I have been able to put every cord in this that I need to with more room for a few more cords. I have to say that this is really helpful for me and it has completely cleaned up my cord rack.

THE BOTTOM LINE
This is just what I needed to store extra cords I don't use as often but still have them handy.

MY RATING
FIVE STARS. This is a great case. It is good for my purposes of storage in my home, but in travel, it would also be a great case to take with you.
text_fidelity_b: DearHomie Cable Organizer Bag,Electronic Accessories Case Portable Double Layer Electronics Organizer Travel Cable Storage Bag for SD Card Charger,Flash Drive,Phone,Cord

text_fidelity_a: PSB Alpha P5 Bookshelf Speaker - Black Ash I am very happy with these speakers.  They are hooked up to the vinyl player, an 80's Harmon Kardon, with a Cambridge Audio amp.  The sound is very clean with a nice bass, but not too much; many modern speakers tend to over-emphasize this.  Back in the day, weight was the measure of all things audio; the heavier the better.  Speakers, amp, you name it.  Not so today with transistors and microprocessors and whatnot, great things can be achieved in lightness.  That said, these speakers have a surprising heft, at maybe ten pounds per, beefy for a bookshelf set.  Being in an apartment, I can't really crank the snot out of these, but get the feeling they will be quite effective on a Friday night sometime when I've had one too many and feel a primordial session of rasping Waits coming on.

text_fidelity_a:
Case Logic Bryker Convertible Backpack (BRYBP114) I travel quite a bit and many of the trips I take are short in duration- often only two or three nights. I don’t need a lot of luggage space for these short trips and I like taking backpacks because I can often avoid carry- on and baggage fees if my backpack can fit under my seat. This desire for economical travel led me to get the Case Logic BRYBPR116 Bryker Backpack Roller.

With this Case Logic Backpack, you get a two-in-one backpack and piece of luggage well suited for travel or business. The wheels make it perfect for traversing an airport and with the added straps, you can carry it on your back, like a traditional backpack. There is an outside pocket where you can tuck the straps so they are not hanging out, flopping around when you don’t need them. And the handle can be completely pushed inside the backpack and sealed off with a zipper so that no one sees it. I like these qualities because it means I can make this look like a backpack when I want it to and I can make it look more like a piece of luggage when I want it to.

Inside the backpack, there is a separate compartment for a laptop and I like that you can unsnap this if you like, making for a larger interior space that is just right for stuffing your two- day supply of clothing and personal items. Like I said, my primary usage with this backpack is for travel and I usually don’t take my laptop with me when I’m on a two- day trip, so I would rather have the open space, to make it more like a piece of luggage.

There is one thing to keep in mind if you take this backpack on a plane, and that is the size of pack makes it only barely able to fit under your seat. It will stick out some, so be prepared to have a snug space where your feet normally go. And unlike other backpacks, it’s too rigid- thanks to the handle- to make it collapsible and flexible. To save having to pay carry- on fees on certain airlines, I am willing to place it under the airline seat in front of me regardless, even if it does stick out some. If your flying on an airline that doesn’t charge extra for carry-ons, then this won’t be an issue since you can easily place the backpack in the overhead, which is what I recommend doing. For everyone else, just bear in mind that the length of the backpack makes it a challenge to fit under a seat.

I have a wide assortment of backpacks and luggage in my home to accommodate different needs. This Case Logic rolling backpack is a nice addition to my collection and I like that it performs a dual role. It has suited me well so far and it makes a good choice of luggage/backpack for business people and others who are constantly on the go for short spans of time.
text_fidelity_b: Case Logic Bryker Convertible Backpack (BRYBP114)

text_fidelity_a:
JOBY UltraFit Sling Strap for Women Horribly Uncomfortable.

What's the one thing that makes a good neck strap comfortable for long term wearing? Padding. What's the one thing this strap is completely lacking? Padding!

The part of the strap that's supposed to go around your neck is a two inch wide very rough textured bit of nylon webbing. Seat belts are softer than this material. The first time I tried the Joby UltraFit Sling Strap I carried my Kodak Z990 around for about an hour and it was so uncomfortable. Who designs a neck strap with NO padding?

This strap attaches to your camera via the ¼" tripod screw mount on the bottom of the camera. It's odd that your camera hangs upside down and I don't like the single point of failure mounting. Also, because of the way it's designed it puts angular force on the mounting threads when hanging and even more when releasing or engaging the quick release latch. Since the threads in my Kodak are plastic I have even more dislike for this mounting system. Additionally, you have to dismount your strap any time you want to use a tripod or monopod.

I found in the time I used this that the only time the (non) padded portion of the strap is on your neck is when the rig is retracted when you use the 'Speed Cinch' to bring the camera up for shooting, at least on my extra large frame, the whole strap rotates forward and puts the even more uncomfortable thinner strap around your neck and the 'padded' section down on your chest.

To sum it up... it's uncomfortable. It completely lacks any padding. It has an odd mounting system that puts lever like force on your tripod socket and you have to take the strap off to use a tripod or monopod. The only good point to this system is that it is rather well made. Unfortunately it's just well made junk. I wouldn't recommend this to anyone for any application.
text_fidelity_b: JOBY UltraFit Sling Strap for Women

RHA MA750 (Discontinued by Manufacturer) I dislike reviews where the comments just gush about the product. But I have no other choice but to do just that - these are some incredibly good earphones!

I've been using RHA earphones for a couple of years and have been impressed by the sound quality given the price. I own several earphones, but the ones I reach for most often by far are my RHA MA350s even though they are one of the least pricey pair of buds I own. Great sound quality and excellent build quality.

Well, the MA350s will be spending some time on the shelf. The MA750s are a clear step up. (Gush alert:) These are simply amazing! They can handle anything I thrown at them so far, with great bass that doesn't boom or bottom out, clear midrange and sharp upper range. Just fantastic performance.

I was a bit concerned about the ear wrap design since I usually find that type of design to be irritating for long-term use, and especially irritating when wearing them while exercising. But no problems at all even with extended wearing. Very comfortable and no chafing even when running.

The MA750s come with an extensive set of replacement ear cushions in a variety of designs. I can't imagine that a person would not be able to adjust these to fit perfectly given there are 10 different potential configurations. The cord is stout but flexible, with significant reenforcements at the plug end.

Even the packaging is upscale, with a high quality box with a front panel (with a magnetic enclosure) that opens to revel the earphones and tips nicely displayed. Very Apple-esque in their presentation.

Also included is a leather (or what feels like leather) carry case. The tips come with a metal holder that fits into the case so you can keep everything neatly stored and protected. A small point, but is shows that some real thought went into every aspect of this product.

While these are priced higher than other RHA earphones, the cost is well worth it. Even at the current price point, these outperform my Bose, Shure and Sennheiser earbuds that are priced far higher, and way outperform buds in their MA750 price range.

Huge recommendation for these - try as I might, I just can't find a single criticism to voice about them.
[Sample provided for review]
text_fidelity_b: RHA MA750 (Discontinued by Manufacturer)

text_fidelity_a:
Garmin nüvi 1350LMT 4.3-Inch Portable GPS Navigator (Discontinued by Manufacturer)) I drive in and around the Boston area, where none of the streets run north/south or east/west, every other intersection is a rotary, and a wrong turn down a one way street can take you an hour to correct.

The Nuvi is slightly better than trying to drive with a map on your steering wheel. I have been using mine for awhile now, and it mostly gets me where I want to go.

The problem is mostly how it does it. As many have already noted, there is no easy way to get it to show you alternate routes. And out of the city, especially, the route it gives you can be full of surprises. Take you off the highway and onto a dirt road for no reason whatsoever surprises. That happened to my husband on his way to a job in Hartford.

And forget trying to get around traffic. I was using it to get home from a doctor's office and saw that there was a ton of traffic on the route it was giving me through Harvard Square, so I turned toward another way home - one I do not know as well, but I know it is possible to get home that way - expecting the Nuvi to tell me it was recalculating and give me my next turn.

It did so, and I turned and followed the directions each time as it - get this - took me into the Harvard Business School parking lot and then out onto a one way street that put me on a no-turning-back 100% committed course to the traffic in Harvard Square.

Thanks, Nuvi.

text_fidelity_a:
Marware Revolve Portrait and Landscape Standing Case for Kindle Fire HD 8.9", Black (will not fit HDX models) Overall, this is a fine case for the 8.9 inch Fire HD. The overall quality is quite nice - I have other Marware products for my Kindle Touch, and it's good to see that they are continuing to maintain a strong focus on product quality. All the materials feel nice; the stitching is tight and even; there's ample cushioning for tablet protection while maintaining a slim profile; and the elastic strap holds the cover closed in a secure fashion.

I also like how Marware packages their products with a minimum of packaging waste but still ensures the product can travel through the mail without being dinged up. The package is also easy to open - no fuss, no muss.

I initially had some difficulty getting the Fire into the case. The Fire is held in place using a plastic cradle, but it seemed to be too small. I had to (gasp!) resort to reading the user guide that came with it, and found out I needed to position it in a certain way and then snap it in. When it is properly inserted you'll hear and feel a clear "snap" at each of the four corners of the tablet. When properly installed the case holds the tablet very securely. I shook it vigorously (over a thick cushion in case it failed) and the Fire stayed put.

My main quibble is with the rotation feature. I was really looking forward to this since some apps only run in portrait mode; others only in landscape. While the rotation feature works, it is very stiff - you really have to twist hard to get it to rotate. It's a two-handed operation: one hand to rotate the tablet; the other to hold the case while you're turning.

The bottom of the cradle has a tab that fits into a slot on the base of the cover to prop up the tablet. This works in both landscape and portrait modes. There are three tabs so you can adjust the angle.

There are cut outs for the power and HDMI ports. I had no problems accessing any of the ports, power button or volume controls while it was in the cover.

Since I often end up having to charge the Fire while it is in use, I rotated the screen so the power plug is at the top. That allows me to keep the tablet propped up on my desk in landscape mode for video watching, but still use the power cord.

It also offers an auto on/off ability - the Fire turns off when you close the cover, and wakes up when you open the cover. It's a nice feature and it works well.

It has a slot on the cover so you can fit your hand into it for ease of holding it. That has value, but what I would have preferred to have instead (or in addition to) is a pocket on either the inside or the outside to hold items such as a cleaning cloth. This is not a huge problem, but I'll certainly miss that since the case for my original Fire has a outside pouch that is great for holding a cleaning cloth and a small stylus.

I'm going to give this 5 stars, but 4.5 is more accurate given the reluctance of the rotation feature. But, since it does everything else very well, looks good, and feels nice, it's closer to a 5 rating than a 4.
text_fidelity_b: Marware Revolve Portrait and Landscape Standing Case for Kindle Fire HD 8.9", Black (will not fit HDX models)

Universal Smart Battery Charger Mark II For AA AAA C D 9V Li-on Ni-MH Ni-Cd Rechargeable Household Batteries With USB Charger Cell Port More than anyone, I really wanted alkaline charging to work like other rechargeable batteries but the sad reality is that they're just not made for it.

The reality of alkaline charging:
- Duracells seem to leak more than cheapo "Kirkland" brand from Costco.
- Energizers do not hold charge very well.
- All brands leak eventually.
- Takes a long time to charge.
- Unreliable even if successfully recharged -- usually, batteries are connected in series, which means that if one fails, the device will not work.
- Battery leak can happen while charging or while being used in the device, resulting in a very messy charger and messy device.

So after some dumpster diving (or at least, I raided the battery recycling bins at work), I came home with batteries of various brands. For a while, I really did use recharged alkaline batteries exclusively and kept my Ni-MH batteries in the drawer. What I found was that I needed to change the batteries a lot more often and I couldn't be sure that the battery would have a charge when I took it out of the drawer.

Leaking is a big problem. My charger now has one charging port that is stuck because the liquid got in to the spring mechanism and dried. I also have a couple of remotes and devices that had to be cleaned out because the batteries leaked.

In the end, I had to give up on the idea of recharging cheap alkaline batteries because of how long it takes to recharge and that it can leak at any time, potentially ruining your device (mostly, it's just oily and you need to clean it out with a tissue). I just couldn't trust those batteries.

So why did I still give this charger 5 stars? Although alkaline charging was a failed experiment for me, the charger is still a better-than-average Ni-MH battery charger. It has separate intelligent charging and LCD display for each battery and will trickle charge a battery even after the lights turn green. Other chargers that have the same features cost more -- and without the Alkaline charging capability. You really can't go wrong with this charger.
text_fidelity_b: Universal Smart Battery Charger Mark II For AA AAA C D 9V Li-on Ni-MH Ni-Cd Rechargeable Household Batteries With USB Charger Cell Port

It actually does seem to help the quality of its audio. It allows me to have clearer sound on my phone for bass in particular, which is something I otherwise find to be a problem when listening to music on my phone. The sound of bass guitar is generally weak without this amplifier. The problem is, in order to use this amplifier with my phone, I have only two choices: (1) Sit still, since it is not possible to freely move around with my phone while listening to music using headphones and this amplifier as I can do when I use Bluetooth earbuds, since this device does not have Bluetooth transmitter capability. (2) Carry my phone in one pocket and this device in a separate pocket, which seems like a weird way to do things in this era of ubiquitous wireless transmission.

Due to the above limitations, this amplifier is much better suited to stationary use, such as a laptop. When I used it that way, it did make both treble and base sound better, and it reduced outside noise.

iHome Smart Brief: 13 inch Laptop Briefcase for Mac, Heathered Grey This is advertised as a 'sleeve for a 13" laptop' which is such an understatement. Not only will this hold a laptop up to 14 inches, it also has compartments for a cell phone, an IPad or other tablet device (my Kindle fits in there quite nicely) and all the necessary chargers and earphones, making this a one stop transportation and storage device for all personal electronics. There is even a bit of room left over to tuck a newspaper, or a file or two. And, unlike most sleeves, this has handles and an optional shoulder strap.

The compartments are zippered so things should not spill out too easily (although I would open the compartment holding the chargers cautiously). It is a nice, neutral grey color that should not make anyone feel self conscious about carrying it and seems to be reasonably durable. The various compartments seem to be adequately padded against the normal traumas (I don't think I would count on it to protect my computer if it were dropped).

There are a few issues though. First since it is not a typical sleeve it probably would not easily fit into a backpack. Second, fully loaded with a computer, phone, tablet and chargers it will be heavy enough that handling this plus a backpack or briefcase during a commute could be awkward. Third, having everything in one spot could be convenient for travelers except dragging everything out to go through TSA and then repacking it would be time consuming.

Overall this is a great product.
text_fidelity_b: iHome Smart Brief: 13 inch Laptop Briefcase for Mac, Heathered Grey

text_fidelity_a:
Panasonic HomeHawk Window Home Monitoring Camera for Outdoor Monitoring, Mounts to Inside Window, Color Night Vision, Wide Angle, 24/7 Full HD Recording, Person Detection, Alexa Compatible KX-HNC500 I've used cheap Wyze cameras as well as more expensive cameras like Arlo in my garage, but wi-fi is pretty iffy there. I wanted to see if the wi-fi receiver in this HomeHawk beats the Wyze or Arlo, but unfortunately, that's not the case. The HomeHawk struggled in my garage as much as the others did. As a matter of fact, I couldn't connect to it at all. So right off the bat, that is something to note... that paying more for a camera doesn't necessarily mean better wi-fi receivers are inside the camera. This isn't something I'm going to subtract a star for since no cameras on the market can help with my wi-fi situation, that's something that will have to be remedied by wi-fi extenders.

Now once I move this camera indoor, with better wi-fi reception, to monitor the backyard, it does the job wonderfully! The app is great and full of features. Be sure you select the proper MODE. By default, it was on BASIC and it did not do any recordings. I realize I had to change it to PROTECTION mode or 24/7 mode. Or, better yet, you can create your own mode! You can determine if it will record 24/7, or only when it detects motion. You can determine the duration of the clip. Now that is pretty cool! The default is 10 seconds, and for several weeks I thought I had to live with the default, until I discovered that I can actually change this by creating my own Mode. You can determine if it will notify you for every motion detected, or only for human detections. Lastly, you can name the mode anything you want, then select it and you're set! I've only used Wyze, Arlo and Homehawk cameras, and without a doubt, this Panasonic software is the best of the bunch. 5-stars!
text_fidelity_b: Panasonic HomeHawk Window Home Monitoring Camera for Outdoor Monitoring, Mounts to Inside Window, Color Night Vision, Wide Angle, 24/7 Full HD Recording, Person Detection, Alexa Compatible KX-HNC500

Samsung Electronics UN49KS8000 49-Inch 4K Ultra HD Smart LED TV (2016 Model) I was hesitant to buy a TV online but went to several local stores and many were out of stock since they were transitioning to 2017 models. So I decided to try Amazon on this 2016 Samsung that had many good reviews and was a good price. I was very impressed with both the TV and the delivery from Amazon.
Delivery: I was able to select which day I wanted it delivered and then was kept updated on the delivery status by Amazon. The delivery company called a few days in advance to verify a 3 hour window of time, and they did arrive that day within the window of time even though it was 10 min prior to the end of that time. They brought the TV in, removed it from the boxing, placed it on our TV stand, plugged it in and verified it was functioning. They took a picture of the functioning TV and took the old box/trash away. I was very pleased with the delivery.
The TV: It is great! Have only used the TV for four days but it has been used a lot during that timeframe. We replaced an older Samsung flatscreen (HD TV) with this one and wow, what a difference. Out of the box without any tuning whatsoever this is a great looking deep colored screen. With a few tweaks it is amazing. There were easy step-by-step onscreen setup instructions. The remote is lot better than the older large clunky devices and is a smart remote that even recognizes voice commands. I liked the concept of having just one cable to the TV which then links to a hub where you plug in other devices. Only issue I had was the TV remote could not recognize my Tivo device from my cable provider for all functions, but it did change channels and volume. I use a generic remote anyway which worked great with the new TV. The bezel is very small and the thickness of the TV is perfect for us.
Overall I was impressed with this TV and would highly recommend it, especially at the discounted price. I’ve already seen reviews of the 2017 version of this TV and some are not very favorable so I'm glad I bought this one.

But, because of the circumstances they would give me a full refund. So, if you buy the watch, and purchase Apple care you will NOT automatically get a refund for Apple care if you change your mind.

If I have a problem.

!OLD REVIEW!

I was aided in this task by two things, 1) I have more fine motor skills than he does and a lot more experience with tiny detail work (painting, beading, etc) and 2) I have fingernails, real ones not acrylic (I think acrylic nails would be too thick).

I used the thin edge of my fingernail to seat the bottom of the nano in the case after sliding it top first under the rubber part at the top of the clip case.

Once it was in my iPod did appear to be very secure. The carabina clip is a bit of an exaggeration, it isn't nearly as sturdy as a carabiner, the like of which is used by climbers, this is more of a jewelry version and feels very lightweight, I'm not pleased with that.

I paid $8 more for the clip aspect of this case and the clip is there but isn't as functional and sturdy as I'd hoped.

The second fail for this case is that the rubber casing covers part of the headphone port.

I bought this case along with my new iPod, so once I'd unpacked both, I loaded a new audiobook onto my new iPod and slipped the case on and decided to take a listen. Nothing.

I couldn't hear anything at all. It was so disappointing. For a moment I thought that my new iPod was defective. Nope.

It turns out that there wasn't enough room for the headphone jack to make a complete connection unless you peeled back the case wall and held it in place while listening.

So annoying.

Anyways, I have a x-acto knife and have been debating whether or not to modify the bottom of the case myself (the clip isn't great and it kinda ticks me off that I have to act as seamstress for this failure of a product if I want to use it). But sending stuff back is tedious and time consuming (okay, it takes about five minutes to return stuff on Amazon, but still, I don't want to do it!).

(OLD MODEL) Seagate Expansion 3TB Desktop External Hard Drive USB 3.0 (STBV3000100) So far, the hard drive is working as one would expect. As always with these things, the questions mostly arise in longevity/reliability issues, so I'll be updating this once I've had a longer time to determine how it does in those categories. First impressions at this point, though:

1) the drive has a relatively small footprint, which is nice

2) Feels quite sturdy and hefty (it's surprisingly heavy) with good build quality

3) This isn't powered by your USB, so you'll need an outlet for its enclosed power cord

4) When you start up, it takes a little while (a few seconds) for the display light to come on. At first, I thought it hadn't started up at all, but just wait a small bit and it will light up

5) the display light is located on top but at the rear of the device, which while minor, is a slight inconvenience. I have it under my desk set back a little ways, so to see the light isn't as immediate as one might like

6) the drive is quite quiet. Not silent--you can hear it--but definitely quieter than many I've had

7) the drive is pretty fast, with the uptick from USB 2 to 3 very noticeable as I move from one computer (USB 2) to the other (USB 3)--it varies depending on what I'm copying, but sometimes the difference is half the speed

8) despite the small footprint, with its necessity for power and it's weight, I wouldn't consider this at all a portable drive, though I suppose you could use it as such. But really, it's big and heavy for that.

9) I use this on several Macs--no problem at all reformatting it for those computers--just a few mouse clicks and a few seconds is all

So far, this is a good big backup drive (I have the 5 TB version). And since we all know, or should, that drives will fail, you can't have too many of them. If any issues arise over time, I'll update accordingly

NETGEAR Orbi Whole Home Tri-band Mesh WiFi 6 System (RBK752) – Router with 1 Satellite Extender | Coverage up to 5,000 sq. ft., 40 Devices | AX4200 (Up to 4.2Gbps) This is the first mesh system I've used. I had a Linksys router and an Asus router before this, both installed with third-party firmware. After the Asus upgrade, I used the Linksys router as a repeater. The signal was okay; considering I had Xfinity 250Mbps, the Asus worked fantastically, while the Linksys trailed behind. We live in an old apartment building with thick, plaster walls, so signal can be very spotty.

With this mesh system, I saw a huge upgrade the first week. Setup was very easy; quick instructions are provided. As soon as the setup was complete, I delved into the firmware. I recall being a little disappointed as I was used to the Asus custom firmware (Asuswrt-Merlin). The Asus firmware "just werqed." I run a small server, and setup was super easy with the Asus. With the Netgear, it was a lot more involved. Setting up outside ports was a pain; at the time, there was no simple way of forwarding ports. I recall a little workaround I was able to conduct with the server, but it took me days to figure out.

The firmware also lacks time restrictions for devices (at least of this writing). Asuswrt-Merlin allows me to set specific times to shut off internet for devices, which comes in handy with a large family.

As for the actual mesh system, so far so good. I can't tell when I'm using the main router or the satellite. The devices connect automatically without hiccup. I've since ditched Xfinity in favor of RCN 1Gbps; this mesh system works very well with the service. Once we have fiber, I can't wait to see the results.
text_fidelity_b: NETGEAR Orbi Whole Home Tri-band Mesh WiFi 6 System (RBK752) – Router with 1 Satellite Extender | Coverage up to 5,000 sq. ft., 40 Devices | AX4200 (Up to 4.2Gbps)

text_fidelity_a: Optiarc AD-5290S-PLUS 24X SATA Internal DVD Optical Drives Burner with 8.7GB Overburn for XGD3 Support (Black) In order to try the over burn feature, I would need the appropriate disks that can normally hold 8.5 GB (DVD+R).  These disks are not too difficult to find online, but the office supply stores only seem to stock 4.7 GB disks.  I guess you either have to special order or buy online.  Most everything that I need to burn can either fit on a 4.7 GB DVD or can be compressed (without much loss of quality) to fit.  It may be false economy to buy the higher capacity disks, as they are nearly double the price of lower capacity.  With burnable media prices being so low anyway, you don't gain much by squeezing as much as you can on a particular disk.  So why did I get this drive?  I like to have a drive on the shelf if one goes bad (and they do sometimes), and then I don't have to wait for one to arrive.  I assumed it was probably good to have one that can burn to maximum capacity as this isn't much more expensive than a regular DVD burner.  Since I haven't actually installed or used the drive yet (waiting for disks), one should not pay as much attention to my review as some other reviewers.  I just wanted people to be aware that you can't insert a 4.7 GB disk and expect to over burn to 8.7 GB.  You need to understand the differences in available media and get the appropriate blank media. Update:  I finally received the appropriate media to test the drive.  It seemed to work good for the first 6 or 8 disks, but then 3 disks in a row had burn errors.  Bad media?  I don't think so; it appears the drive is failing already.  I'll test on another computer and see if it is the media or the drive and update the review again, but right now I can't recommend this drive at all.  UPDATE 2:  I tried this again after rebooting my computer and it now seems to work fine and does indeed overburn, so you can squeeze a lot on one disk.  When I had 3 bad burns in a row, I thought it was the burner, but it may have been bad media.  On the other hand, I suspect something flaky on my PC, as I have had bad burns before occasionally (not recently) and then after a reboot everything was fine again.  I may have too many programs loaded when I try to burn.  That's not the fault of the DVD drive.  Most likely the fault of the burning program (and I am using a major well-know program.)
text_fidelity_b: Optiarc AD-5290S-PLUS 24X SATA Internal DVD Optical Drives Burner with 8.7GB Overburn for XGD3 Support (Black)

LotFancy 7 Inch 16:9 TFT Color LCD Widescreen Car Rear View Monitor Bundle with Remote and Waterproof Camera I received this as a free review sample five months ago and have been using it for around four months. This is a rear view monitor only - not a dashcam - and it works far better than one of the combination rear monitors/dashcams that I have also used.

Since there are a large number of reviews that cover this in detail I am going to keep mine brief. Here is the single thing I do not like about it: the terrible documentation. On the other hand you can have this professionally installed for not a lot of money, which is the route that I took. If you are a do-it-yourselfer installing it right is less than an hour job (according to the tech who installed mine).

What I love is the clear visual behind me. The camera works in dark and low light, and the display has sufficient clarity and resolution to easily see what is behind you and estimate distances. If you were to purchase this as an option on a vehicle I shudder to think of the cost, but for less than one hundred fifty bucks professionally installed this is a bargain. And if you do install it yourself you can knock a C-note off that cost.

If you parallel park frequently this is a perfect way to make that easier. For rural driving this may not be a needed accessory, but for city use it's a convenience (and a safety feature as well.) Do note the information in the product specs too because they are clear about what this will and will not work with.

text_fidelity_a:
Garmin 4.3-Inch Carrying Case Bought this for the 750 because it didn't come with a case. A similar (smaller) case came with my 360 and I didn't think this purchase through. After using it and comparing the other cases out there, I would buy a different case.

This slipcase for the 750 fits tight. That's good. The Nuvi won't slip out. But because the 750's on/off switch is now a slider on the top left corner, if you slide it into the case naturally (unit in your right hand, case in your left) the switch rubs against the case. When you pull the unit out, it "automatically" turns on. Thus if you were to pull the unit out partially then push it back in, you could turn it on and not know it.

The solution is to invert the Nuvi so its switch will be at the open end of the case after it's in the case. That way you can see the switch's on/off position and verify it's not on.

More practical issues:

Pros:

- Nicely made: very high quality

- Very compact

- Adequate protection against rattling inside a glove compartment or briefcase

- Good basic case

Cons:

- It can accidentally turn the unit on

- It's black: can't find it easily in the dark buried at the bottom of my shoulder bag when traveling. Experienced this with the 360's case. And if it falls on the floor of a rental car at night, good luck trying to find it. Wish it came in natural leather color.

- Offers no protection while hand holding the unit while walking

The [[ASIN:B0012MI7N2 Garmin Nuvi 800 Series Carrying Case]] case is a wallet style that flips open to reveal the screen. It stays on the unit during use and offers some protection if you dropped your Nuvi on the sidewalk while walking. Downside with that unit appears to be that the cover flap does not latch, allowing the case to flip open in a briefcase and the screen to be scratched by other junk. And it's also black and can get lost on a car floor.

Another alternate is one of the many zippered semi-rigid or neoprene cases.
text_fidelity_b: Garmin 4.3-Inch Carrying Case

text_fidelity_a:
Tascam TH-02 Closed Back Studio Headphones, Black [Great Sound]

As noted in some of the other reviews this pair of headphones has great sound for its price range. Sound is quite neutral, without the bass emphasis of a lot of headphones at this range. Highs are also good and not muted. The cable is also very generous in length, which is great as my computer is far away from my chair. Finally, the headband adjustment is exceptional. I have a fairly large skull and most headphones I've purchased have not fit well. However, this one fits perfectly and even has more room to expand. The only comfort downside is that the pads have quite a stiff covering material. This is not so great for comfort for long use sessions, but not too big of an issue as you can replace them eventually if needed. The thicker pad material would make the headphones last longer...if it were not for the major issue I describe below with build quality.

[Disappointing Build Quality]

I've had my pair for about 1.5 years now, and today the headphone snapped at the joint between the top band and where the extension band slides out. See attached photo. You can see that there is a metal band in the headband to provide elasticity and resistance. But the extension band (the part that slides in and out) doesn't have a metal band inside of it. This concentrates stress at this transition point, causing the plastic to snap here eventually. I noticed that the plastic on the other cup has also started cracking. The plastic itself feels quite brittle and is about as thick as the metal strip in the headband. I think the fact that I have a large head and had to extend the headphones out only hastened their demise as this put more stress on the plastic-only part of the headbands.

[Conclusion]

This is a great sounding pair of headphones for their price, but alas I cannot recommend them anymore due to the snapping of the headband. To fail after about a year of use is a bit on the low end. My previous pair of similarly priced headphones lasted over 10 years without the headband failing (only cable had become worn). I think you *might* be OK if you have a smaller head and don't have to extend the headphone band too much, but if you have to expand it to near its maximum, it will probably snap off like mine did.
text_fidelity_b: Tascam TH-02 Closed Back Studio Headphones, Black

. Actually, from the time I took it out of the box to the time I was listening to the first CD in it, was about 20 minutes (with the Blue tooth connected by then too). I shared some photos with a CD beside the player in this review so you can compare how big it is. The volume for my 2 bedroom condo is great, wouldn't need anything any louder, and it's clear sound (even with the likely very cheap speakers I have right now). So far, it's only Day 1 having it, but no complaints so far. Nicely, had just received an offer for Amazon Prime the same day, so have been using the blue tooth to take advantage of that. If you need a player that won't skip during an earthquake, this seems to be the one.

I tried playing a CD recorded using Windows Media Player, a variety of song copied down from YouTube put to CD, and the CD worked fine. Was also able to insert a USB stick with Music copied to it from the computer and with the help of the Very Rapid Response Customer Service was enabled to work through a 'glitch' on my end in regard to how the player reads music stored on the USB device (which happens to be , 'a separate folder for each ripped CD' )

Sound quality is pretty good out-of-the-box, but a little thin at the higher frequencies (especially noticeable with acoustic music). Fortunately, Jaybird has a great smartphone app you can use to equalize the sound. I was never very good at designing my own equalization profiles by ear, but the app has several ready made profiles so I just picked the one that sounded best with my favorite music (boosting higher frequencies more than lower frequencies). There is no noise cancellation, but noise isolation is very good with the included foam eartips (not the default eartips).

I really do not like that you need a special dongle to recharge this headset. You can't just plug a standard USB cable directly into these, like with most Bluetooth headset. This may have something to do with the headset's waterproof rating, but other headsets I own are also waterproof and can still be recharged with a standard cable. I am concerned that the proprietary charging dongle will get lost or broken or I will just forget to bring it with me when traveling.
text_fidelity_b: Jaybird X4 Wireless Bluetooth Headphones for Sport Fitness and Running, Compatible with iOS and Android Smartphones: Sweatproof and Waterproof - Black Metallic/Flash

text_fidelity_a:
PIONEER Truly Wireless in-Ear Headphones, Black, SE-C8TW(B) If you're an iphone user, you're probably wondering whether to buy these Pioneer wireless headphones or the Apple version. The Pioneer price is about 1/3 cheaper than Apple. The Pioneer earbuds fit in your ear, so you get much better sound and much better sound isolation. These are nowhere near as detailed or loud as similarly priced wired headphones, but that's true of all wireless Bluetooth earbuds. I will say the connection is stable and not noisy, so these are better than most cheap Bluetooth earbuds. There is some bass, but don't work well for bass-heavy music. Maximum volume is just OK. Battery life is only about 3 hours per charge (compared to 5 hours for Apple), then you have to put the earbuds back in the case for a 1 hour charge. 3 hours may be enough for you; you have to decide, but 5 hours is certainly going to be more interesting to most people. The charging case is much larger than the Apple charging case. The case is 3.3 inches long and 2.2 inches wide. These case is to big to fit comfortably in my pants pocket, so I would only carry it with me in a backpack or purse.

Usage is pretty simple. They paired easily with my phone as a normal Bluetooth device. The buttons on the headphones are easy to use. They are comfortable in my ears. They are secure enough so far, never feeling like they are going to fall out. They are not noticeably heavy like some earbuds can be. When in my ears, they are much less ugly than the Apple earbuds.

I would give these 5 stars for the price and performance if the sound and battery life were better. Frankly, I've tried a few different totally wireless earbuds and been less than impressed by all of them. Bluetooth headphones that have a wire connecting the two pieces can be had for much lower prices and have much better sound quality and much better battery life. Removing the wire just doesn't seem worth the downsides to me.
text_fidelity_b: PIONEER Truly Wireless in-Ear Headphones, Black, SE-C8TW(B)

TP-Link AV1200 Powerline Ethernet Adapter - Gigabit Port, Plug&Play, Power Saving(TL-PA8010 KIT) Ordered at 7am PDT
Received at 5pm PDT
Plugged it in with the very very simple 6 step instruction. Don't let this fool you though. It's as easy as plugging in a cord into an outlet.
( note: do not use a power strip. It must be plugged directly into the wall.

No additional configuration was necessary. it just started working.

background: I needed this for my ps4, which is about 40 feet away from the router and hits 2-3 walls. I get about 300Mbps with Spectrum, but down at the 2.4 frequency. I can receive about 40-50Mbps depending on the strength of the the radio card on the device. The original PS4 wifi card is notorious for being extremely poor in quality. I was receiving about 2Mbps down and 599Kbps up. Yes, you read that right. a modern PS4 on a 2.4 frequency was getting shitty thruput. While at the same time, my other devices on a 2.4 frequency were receiving 10x that, even more on a 5g frequency.

I plugged in this unit and immediately got 10Mbps down and 5Mbps up. It's not a game changer, but will suffice.
Update after 12 hours: Reset the modem and did another speed test on the ps4. 25Mbps down and 10Mbps up.

text_fidelity_a:
Creative Technology Speaker - for Portable use - USB This speaker set sounds great for its size. The sound is loud and clear, but also full in the way you would expect stereo sound to be. It is also small enough to travel fairly easily, although it is not the smallest on the market. This is capable of getting louder than you'll ever be able to use in a hotel room, but suitable for an apartment; there are plenty of options out there in the form of travel speakers.

The built in mic is obviously a significant factor, and it works great compared to my laptop mic. I do like the fact that it gets its power and signal over one cable, but sometimes I think I'm going to run out of USB ports since I use them regularly to charge my phones and other devices. And I was also expecting bluetooth after seeing the ads for the other models. But who cares about bluetooth when you still need power?-smaller speakers don't need an external power source.

This is a good product and I'm certain to use it, especially when travelling for long enough that I want to set up more of a "home" that includes music. It is sort of another take on what is already a niche product, however, and although I do think it's one of the better styles on the market, it's still not the end all of small speakers, nor does it make dramatic improvements over what is already available. It's great at packing full sound into something very portable, and it eliminates one cable if you use USB, but then you use up another USB port. I'd love to see it either fully wireless with included battery or also include a webcam to preclude the need for other accessories. Yes, I know these things would up the cost, but it would make a truly remarkable product.

I also like how the invisible button panel appears when powered on, but not how you can't completely turn it off without removing the power source. The speaker looks good and I like how all sides are covered in speaker screen material, but I worry I could easily stick my finger through a cone.

A quality product that is great if it closely fits your needs.
text_fidelity_b: Creative Technology Speaker - for Portable use - USB

text_fidelity_a:
Belkin VideoLink 3 Powerline Internet Adapter This seemed to be the perfect solution to a problem I was having with obtaining Internet access in my basement. The router is located on the upper floor of the house and, while access is fine in every room above ground, access in the basement has been minimal at best.

Installation was very straightforward - just plug one adapter into the router, the other into the wall socket, and plug in whatever device needs access into one of the three plugs located on the wall socket device.

Overall it works pretty well, but is highly sensitive to noise or heavy draws on the power line. For example, I have a dehumidifier in the basement. When that kicks on, I lose the connection. Sometimes it is regained all by itself, but most of the time I have to either reboot (or power cycle) the device that is plugged in, or unplug and then re-plug the adapter. I tried moving the dehumidifier to a different circuit than the one used by the powerline adapter, and also tried plugging the dehumidifier into a surge protector - no difference. So, I make sure the dehumidifier is off before I use any Internet device.

I've had the same issue with other appliances such as certain vacuums - turn them on, and the connection is lost. There have been no problems with appliances operating in other areas of the house, such as the microwave, laser printers, etc. Just happens when you use the appliance in the same room as the powerline adapter.

But, other than these powerline induced interruptions, the device works well. Speedy connection - can't tell any difference between this and any other WiFi connected device. Well worth taking a look at if you have some WiFi dead zones in your house. Just keep an eye out for someone who is about to use a vacuum when you're at a critical spot in the movie you're streaming!
text_fidelity_b: Belkin VideoLink 3 Powerline Internet Adapter

Camera Tripod Handle for Big Cam - MT- 43 Portable Sturdy Travel Vlog-Style Tripod Small Tabletop Acra Swiss QR Ballhead Tripod Extendable Cold Shoe Handheld for Heavy Camera Mirrors DSLR Digital I mostly like this tripod. It is solidly built and has a lot of useful features, but it also has some shortcomings that prevent me from giving it 5 stars. Here are my most important plusses and minuses:

Plusses:
+ precise construction
+ important components are sturdy metal, especially the ball head and the locking mechanisms that control the center post and the legs
+ folds up compactly for easy travel
+ relatively lightweight compared to solid metal tripods
+ cold shoe is very useful for attaching a microphone or video light

Minuses:
- legs only fold out in one flat position, so this tripod can really only be used on flat level surfaces (like tabletops).
- center post cannot be pushed all the way down below the legs like with most tripods for maximum stability
- selfie-stick mode is only 12 inches long maximum
- $80 price is expensive for a tabletop-only mini-tripod
text_fidelity_b: Camera Tripod Handle for Big Cam - MT- 43 Portable Sturdy Travel Vlog-Style Tripod Small Tabletop Acra Swiss QR Ballhead Tripod Extendable Cold Shoe Handheld for Heavy Camera Mirrors DSLR Digital

ASUS ZenDrive Silver 13mm External 8X DVD/ Burner Drive +/-RW with M-Disc Support, Compatible with both Mac & Windows and Nero BackItUp for Android devices (USB 2.0 & Type-C cables included) Looking back at all the recordable data storage media formats that have fallen by the wayside over the years, I guess it's inevitable that writable CD/DVD will eventually go obsolete too.

And many of our devices don't come with built-in CD/DVD drives these days, since flash drives and cloud storage and downloadable software and streaming video have pretty much taken the load for now.

But some of us still have DVD movie collections and still have an occasional need for a CD/DVD drive. And this is a good one.

It's USB powered and doesn't need an extra power adapter. It comes with two USB cables --- both USB type A (the regular kind) and type C (the newer reversible kind).

Here are a few of the specs:

Read/write speed is 8X for DVDs and 24X for CDs, 4X for DVD video playback.
USB interface is 2.0 (not 3.0).
It's compatible with Window 10, 8, 7, Vista, and XP, and Mac OS X 10.6 and above.
It has M-disc support.

It comes with bundled software for backing up and encryption that you may or may not want to use.
text_fidelity_b: ASUS ZenDrive Silver 13mm External 8X DVD/ Burner Drive +/-RW with M-Disc Support, Compatible with both Mac & Windows and Nero BackItUp for Android devices (USB 2.0 & Type-C cables included)
